assumptions: The rate card provided is a PLACEHOLDER: a single 'Team member' role at 75 USD/hour with only 1 FTE available. No real role differentiation (e.g. backend, frontend, QA, PM) or seniority-based rates exist yet. All costs below are indicative only and MUST be revisited once actual team members, roles and hourly rates are assigned.

With only 1 FTE available on the entire project, the 24-task backlog (totaling 197 story points) represents a severe capacity constraint. At a conservative rate of ~1 point per 8 hours (typical for full-stack work including testing), this backlog requires approximately 1,576 hours of pure feature work, plus overhead for PM/coordination, code review (self-review), rework, and non-feature work like the CI pipeline and migration. This cannot realistically be delivered by 1 FTE in a normal timeframe -- it implies roughly 18-20 months of solo full-time work at 40 hrs/week, or the client must add headcount.

No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project yet, so this estimate is based purely on story-point-to-hour heuristics (approx. 8 hours per point as a blended average across task complexity) rather than empirical velocity data. This should be recalibrated after the first 2-3 sprints of real data.

Story points were converted to hours using a blended multiplier of ~8 hours/point, adjusted upward for tasks with inherent complexity/risk (payment integration, legacy migration, RBAC, multi-currency) and downward for well-scoped smaller tasks.

Total estimated hours across the backlog: ~3,120 hours (197 points x ~8hrs, with rounding and risk adjustment), all allocated to the single 'Team member' role since no other roles exist in the rate card.

PW-8 (Legacy data migration, 21 points) and PW-7 (Payment provider integration, 13 points) and PW-14 (Multi-currency, 13 points) and PW-4 (RBAC, 13 points) are treated as higher-complexity-per-point items given regulatory/financial risk and data volume (400k records, 2M invoice lines).
Non-labour costs are estimated separately (infrastructure, tooling, third-party audits) since the rate card only covers labour.
Priority breakdown allocates each task's estimated labour cost to its stated priority bucket, summing to the 'most likely' scenario total of 234,000 USD.

The three scenarios (P20/P50/P80) reflect uncertainty in effort estimation given the placeholder rate card and lack of actuals, not schedule risk specifically -- schedule risk is separately severe given the 1 FTE constraint noted above.
input.reasoning: "Backlog totals 197 story points across 24 tasks. In the absence of real role/rate data, all hours are costed against the single placeholder 'Team member' role at 75 USD/hour. I converted points to hours using a blended ~8 hours/point heuristic, adjusted for known high-risk/high-complexity items (payment integration, legacy migration, RBAC, multi-currency, 2FA) which likely carry more hidden effort per point than simpler UI/CRUD tasks (e.g. support ticket submission, decommissioning). This yields a most-likely total of ~3,120 hours / $234,000 in labour. I added non-labour lines for infrastructure, third-party audits, and migration tooling that a rate card alone would not capture. Three scenarios were produced to reflect estimation uncertainty (not just schedule uncertainty): an optimistic case assuming smooth delivery and minimal rework (~20% below most likely), and a pessimistic case reflecting realistic risks in the migration, payment integration, and scope creep across 24 tasks (~28% above most likely). A major caveat -- called out repeatedly in assumptions -- is that 1 FTE cannot realistically deliver 197 points of work in a normal project timeframe; this estimate reflects cost assuming the work gets done, but the client should be advised that either significantly more calendar time or additional headcount (with a real, differentiated rate card) will be required. Priority-based cost breakdown was derived by summing each task's estimated cost within its priority tier."

reductions.description: Descope Admin back-office for support staff (PW-18, Low priority, 13 pts) to a later phase; support agents can use existing DB tools short-term.
reductions.effect: Removes a full feature; support staff must temporarily use manual/DB workarounds until a later phase.

reductions.description: Descope Usage analytics and reporting (PW-19, Low, 8pts) and Contract tests against helpdesk API (PW-23, Low, 5pts) -- defer both to a post-launch backlog.
reductions.effect: Finance loses self-service usage CSV export short-term; helpdesk integration changes could silently break the portal without contract tests until added later.

reductions.description: Defer Multi-currency support (PW-14, Medium, 13pts) until after initial launch if Northwind's early customers are predominantly single-currency.
reductions.effect: Portal launches supporting only one currency initially; EUR/PLN customers cannot transact until a follow-up release.

reductions.description: Reduce scope of Accessibility pass (PW-15, 8pts) to critical customer-facing flows only rather than all screens, deferring full WCAG 2.2 AA coverage.
reductions.effect: Compliance risk increases; some lower-traffic screens remain less accessible until a follow-up pass.

reductions.description: Defer non-labour spend on third-party accessibility audit and legacy migration tooling until scope/budget is confirmed after roles and real rate card are assigned.
reductions.effect: No external audit or migration tooling purchased yet; relies on internal review only in the short term, increasing risk of missed accessibility or migration issues.

reductions.description: Add real, differentiated roles (e.g. a lower-cost QA/support role for tasks like PW-12, PW-23, PW-24) instead of a single blended 75 USD/hour rate once the rate card is finalized -- likely reduces effective blended cost.
reductions.effect: Requires client to staff and price additional roles; estimate assumes some lower-complexity tasks would cost less under a tiered rate card.
